findings.evidence: Lines 363–369 define the public `LinearEquiv`, while grep finds application lemmas only for `derivationMulEquivTangentKer` and `derivationAddEquivTangent_symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` lemmas characterizing the linear equivalence in both directions (in particular its second component and inverse evaluation), analogous to lines 316 and 324.
findings.issue: `derivationLinearEquivTangent` has no forward or inverse pointwise characterization, so consumers cannot simplify its application without unfolding its opaque construction; the only new `[simp]` lemma targets the intermediate `derivationAddEquivTangent`.

findings.evidence: The only grep hits for `derivationAddEquivTangent` are its definition, its single lemma, the transported `Module` instance, and construction of `derivationLinearEquivTangent` on lines 342–369.
findings.fix: Make this transport helper private (or inline it) and expose the characteristic lemmas on `derivationLinearEquivTangent` instead.
findings.issue: `derivationAddEquivTangent` duplicates the additive equivalence already exported as `(derivationLinearEquivTangent R A B).toAddEquiv` and otherwise only serves construction of the instance and final linear equivalence.

summary: The exported linear equivalence lacks characteristic simp lemmas, while a redundant intermediate additive equivalence is exposed.
